finding: The country home page's hero and SEO copy comes from a code module (frontend/lib/content/country-home-copy.ts) whose lookup keys mix upper- and lower-case country codes, and whose CMS-vs-code precedence is decided by two inline literals (preferIrelandExtras = code === "ie"; preferSeoExtras adds code === "br"). The EXTRAS map is case-normalised so its Ireland entries work; the BUNDLE map is NOT, so six blocks of reviewed Ireland copy (team H2 'Named doctors.', 'No anonymous rotas.', stats-band labels, how-it-works bodies, final CTA) render nothing on production today.
proposed_fix: One per-country home-copy record (PageContent HOME rows, or lib/content/countries/<code>.json behind one loader) plus a Country.homeCopySource field ('cms_first'|'code_first') replacing both inline literals. Lowercase the lookup key at construction and type it, so a mis-cased key is a compile error rather than silent nothing.
acceptance_test: curl /ireland/en and assert the page contains 'Named doctors.' and 'No anonymous rotas.'; curl each of the six market homes and assert H1 and <title> are unchanged from the 2026-09-15 baseline recorded in country_coupling.csv; grep the repo for 'preferIrelandExtras' and expect zero hits.
rollback: Revert the loader commit; EXTRAS/BUNDLE literals are untouched by the fix so the previous render returns immediately.
follow_up_measurement_window: 14 days - GSC impressions/CTR for the six market home URLs, plus a Search Console query check on 'online doctor ireland'.

finding: The localized country name (common.countryNames[code], present for all six codes in every locale bundle) is used only when code === "br". Every other market prints the English DB seed name inside localized copy: /czechia/cs/doctors/dr-ahmed-maklad serves '<title>MUDr. Ahmed Maklad | Prakticky lekar online v Cesku - Czechia</title>' and /czechia/cs/services/obnoveni-lecby contains 'Czechia' twice in otherwise-Czech copy. In doctor-profile-page.tsx the correct generic expression already sits five lines below the Brazil-gated one.
proposed_fix: Delete the `code === "br" ?` ternary at all four sites and always use `common.countryNames?.[code] ?? config.name`. Pass `country={code}` unconditionally to VerifiedProfessionals and let its market table decide (it already has BR_PT_COPY and PT_PT_COPY).
acceptance_test: curl /czechia/cs/doctors/dr-ahmed-maklad and assert the title ends '- Cesko', not '- Czechia'; curl /czechia/cs/services/obnoveni-lecby and assert zero occurrences of 'Czechia'; assert /brazil/pt and /ireland/en are byte-identical in their country tokens to the 2026-09-15 baseline.
rollback: One-line revert per site; no data migration.
follow_up_measurement_window: 28 days - GSC impressions for /czechia/cs/doctors/* and /czechia/cs/services/*; watch for a title-rewrite drop in the 'Czechia' brand queries.

finding: Three modules with three different signatures and three different gating conventions do the same job: ireland-static-page-seo.ts (3 pages x 6 locales, gated externally by `code === "ie"`), czechia-static-page-seo.ts (10 page keys, cs only, self-gated), portugal-static-page-seo.ts (2 page keys, pt only, self-gated). Spain, Romania and Brazil have no market SEO for any of these page families and render the generic i18n template: /spain/es/pricing is 'Elija su plan mensual - Espana - Global Health' against Ireland's 'Online GP Membership Plans Ireland | Monthly Care'. A fourth market wanting owned copy needs a fourth module plus edits to up to 11 templates.
proposed_fix: One `staticPageSeo(code, locale, pageKey)` over a single nested record (or the existing PageContent CMS rows keyed by a STATIC page type). Replace 11 named imports with one; delete the three modules once their content is migrated. Also drop the `code === "pt" &&` prefix on pricing/page.tsx line 44 - isCountryFeatureEnabled(config, 'subscriptions') is already the rule.
acceptance_test: curl the 60 (6 markets x 10 page families) static URLs and diff <title>/H1 against the 2026-09-15 baseline: Ireland, Czechia and Portugal must be byte-identical; Spain, Romania and Brazil may only change where new copy was deliberately authored. frontend/tests/unit/ireland-core-page-seo.test.ts and czechia-core-page-seo.test.ts must pass unchanged.
rollback: Keep the three modules in place behind the new loader for one release; reverting is deleting the loader call.
follow_up_measurement_window: 28 days - GSC impressions and average position for the 60 static URLs, split by market.

url_or_template: Admin CMS write path (services, service FAQs, service links, doctors, doctor market profiles, doctor FAQs) - all six markets
finding: backend/src/content/romania-clinical-review.ts is an 81KB module whose exported entry point, reviewedRomaniaTransaction(), wraps every admin CMS write in the product and enforces clinical approval for Romania, Spain AND Brazil from three hardcoded const registries of state hashes. Ireland, Czechia and Portugal CMS writes are ungated. Approval evidence - including one entry reading 'verbal, reported by the owner' - lives in source code with no admin surface. Separately, Czech clinically approved doctor FAQs live in a frontend constant (czechia-approved-doctor-faqs.ts) keyed by doctor slug, and return an EMPTY FAQ list if any approved id is missing from the DB.
proposed_fix: Rename the function to reviewedClinicalTransaction; add Country.clinicalApprovalMode ('off'|'shadow'|'enforce') and a ClinicalApproval table (countryCode, entityKey, stateSha256, reviewerDoctorId, reviewedAt, evidence) that the admin can read. Migrate the three const registries and the Czech FAQ replacements into it. DoctorFaq gains approvedAt/approvedBy.
acceptance_test: backend/src/routes/authz-matrix.test.ts passes; a scripted admin edit to a Romania service is still rejected with RomaniaClinicalApprovalRequiredError (renamed) before migration and its successor after; an edit to an Ireland service is rejected once Ireland is set to 'enforce' and allowed at 'off'; /czechia/cs/doctors/dr-ahmed-maklad still serves 'Jak si rezervovat konzultaci s MUDr. Makladem?'.
rollback: Ship behind clinicalApprovalMode='shadow' first (same pattern as MEDICAL_ACCESS_ENFORCE); flipping back to 'shadow' restores today's behaviour for the three gated markets and no new gate for the other three.
follow_up_measurement_window: One full admin editing cycle (about 30 days) - count rejected writes per market and confirm no false rejections.

finding: Money routing is decided by inline country literals: a switch selects the Stripe account (ie/pt/cz; everything else falls through to Ireland), a literal array ['ie','pt','cz'] enumerates webhook secrets, `countryCode !== "pt"` gates MB Way/Multibanco, and `countryCode === "pt"` appears three times in one file to skip platform invoicing. Every one of these rules is legitimate; none is data. A seventh market silently bills through the Ireland Stripe entity and its webhooks fail signature verification with no error naming the cause.
proposed_fix: Country.stripeAccountKey, Country.checkoutPaymentMethods (string[]) and Country.invoiceIssuer ('platform'|'external') on the Country record; account config read from STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_<CODE> / STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_<CODE> with an Ireland fallback; an issuer registry selects pt-invoicexpress. Delete the switches and the three repeated PT guards.
acceptance_test: A sandbox checkout in each of the six markets routes to the same Stripe account as today (assert on the account id in the session); a PT sandbox checkout still offers mb_way + multibanco and issues no platform invoice; getConfiguredWebhookSecrets() returns the same set.
rollback: Keep the switches as the fallback path for one release, selected only when the Country field is null.
follow_up_measurement_window: One full payout cycle - reconcile per-market settlement against the admin commission-payout report.

finding: The sitemap's lab-test DETAIL loop (app/sitemap.ts around line 191) iterates every country with no feature gate, while the HUB entry 30 lines further down correctly calls isCountryFeatureEnabled(country, 'health-tests') and the page itself calls notFound() on the same check. Result: 84 Ireland /lab-tests/{slug} URLs (14 tests x 6 locales) are submitted to Google and every one returns 404. Romania's 6 hub URLs are the only lab-test URLs that resolve.
